subject: Multi-site resilience questionnaire and runbook extract
messages:
From: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@nebula-fin.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@nebula-fin.com
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: resilience questionnaire + runbook extract for Redwood Inference

Hi Camila,

Thanks for taking this — Nebula is collecting a short set of targeted resilience and recovery questions as part of our vendor RFI. We need a concise response that covers multi-region failover behavior, RTO/RPO expectations, and a short runbook extract showing sequencing for a primary-region outage. Our security and ops teams are particularly focused on:

- Expected RTO for customer-facing inference traffic for hosted API vs. dedicated customers
- RPO for session state and customer-managed data (snapshots vs. streaming replication)
- Model and KV cache rehydration steps and expected cold-start impact
- DNS and routing cutover timing, and whether you support automated health-based failover vs. manual
- Any recommended configuration for prioritizing availability vs. cost (e.g., warm standby, active-active)
- Evidence of encrypted replication, and where logs/audit trails are stored for post-incident review

I've attached a short spreadsheet (Nebula_Resilience_RFI.xlsx) with our checklist to make it easy to map answers. Can you get an initial reply with high-level numbers and a plan for a runbook extract by EOD Tuesday (three business days)? If you have a sample runbook we can review, please include it.

Procurement looped in for timing. Thanks — feel free to call if quicker.

Best,
Ethan Shaw
Lead, Infrastructure Resilience
Nebula Financial

[Attachment: Nebula_Resilience_RFI.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Request: resilience questionnaire + runbook extract for Redwood Inference

Hi Ethan — appreciate the clear checklist. Confirming we can deliver a concise response and a runbook extract by EOD Tuesday. I’m attaching a short summary PDF that covers the high-level answers; we will follow up with a runbook extract and RTO/RPO table.

High-level answers (short):
- Hosted (global API): active-active across two regions by default for stateless inference; automated traffic steering with health probes; expected failover traffic cutover within 1–3 minutes for new requests, with client-observed latency variance for in-flight streaming requests up to ~15s while retrying.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): customers may choose warm-standby cross-region or two-region active-active. SLA-backed Dedicated plans can offer 99.95% availability; typical switchover window for reserved warm standby is 5–20 minutes depending on model cache warmup.
- RPO: user session state stored in a replicated, encrypted datastore (multi-AZ within region + cross-region async replication); for critical session checkpoints we recommend synchronous replication for near-zero RPO (~0–5s). Non-critical telemetry can be recovered from event streams (RPO up to 1–2 minutes).
- KV cache rehydration: automatic prefix/KV cache persistence to replicated object store; cold-cache warmup is typically 30–90s per model shard; we have prioritized prefetch for canary traffic to reduce impact.
- Routing: health-probe-based automated failover using smart routing policies; customers can opt into manual cutover for more control.
- Encryption and audit: replication uses TLS in transit and CMEK for at-rest encryption; audit logs retained in our control plane for 90 days by default, extendable for Dedicated/Private.

We will attach the runbook extract and a simple RTO/RPO table tomorrow. If Nebula prefers, we can highlight the differences between Hosted and Dedicated in a two-column matrix.

Sent from my laptop — happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RI_Resilience_Summary_v1.pdf (pdf, 78KB)]

Subject: Re: Request: resilience questionnaire + runbook extract for Redwood Inference

Ethan — attaching the requested runbook extract and our RTO/RPO table. Below are the concrete answers pulled from the runbook extract; the attached PDF (RI_Runbook_Extract_2027-07-12.pdf) contains step-by-step sequence snippets and exact CLI/console commands we use in region failover drills. The CSV (RTO_RPO_Table_2027-07-12.csv) summarizes the expected windows by product mode.

Summary of concrete commitments and expected windows
- Hosted API (stateless inference)
  - Typical automated cross-region traffic cutover: 1–3 minutes for new requests (DNS + edge routing propagation + health-probe routing).
  - In-flight streaming requests: best-effort reconnection/continuation; clients should expect up to 15–30s interruption unless using streaming-resume tokens.
  - RPO: stateless inference has effectively zero RPO for model artifacts; session state persisted to encrypted replicated store with configurable sync. Default offered: asynchronous cross-region replication (RPO <= 2 minutes); synchronous option for near-zero RPO (0–5s) upon request for sensitive workloads.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity)
  - Warm-standby configuration: target switchover 5–20 minutes (includes model GPU cache warmup and route draining). SLA-backed options with accelerated provisioning (4-hour priority provisioning) available as add-on; SLA language included in Dedicated T&C.
  - Active-active for dedicated customers: continuous cross-region replication and global load balancing; observed cutover under 3 minutes for new sessions if both sides kept warm.

- Data and replication
  - Customer data at rest encrypted with CMEK options; replication over TLS with integrity checks. Audit trails for replication and failover actions are stored in our control plane and mirrored to customer-provided S3 when requested. Standard retention 90 days; extended retention options available.

- Runbook excerpt (high level sequencing)
  1) Detect region failure via health probes and alerting (automated).
  2) Promote secondary routing policy (automated or manual) and progressively shift traffic using weighted routing and canaries.
  3) Initiate KV cache rehydration: prioritized keys for active customers prefetched; full cache warmup proceeds in background.
  4) For dedicated customers, trigger accelerated provisioning if warm standby not kept and customer has priority add-on.
  5) Post-cutover verification and incident audit: check control-plane metrics, compare token costs, and upload incident logs to shared drive.

Attachments and links
- RI_Runbook_Extract_2027-07-12.pdf (runbook snippets, 420KB)
- RTO_RPO_Table_2027-07-12.csv (single-sheet table with per-mode RTO/RPO estimates)
- Drive folder with sample incident logs and drill recordings: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRI-resilience-samples

Next steps
- If Nebula would like language for procurement, we can provide legal-approved SLA phrasing and a short addendum for Dedicated commitments (Rishi/Lauren will supply the approved lines).
- We’re available to run a joint failover drill with Nebula ops — recommend a tabletop walkthrough followed by a simulated failover in a non-prod window.

Thanks — attaching the PDF and CSV now.

Best,
